subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Light vs. Dark Roasts
description: A quick win: understand Light vs. Dark Roasts.

hook.text: Light roasts have more caffeine and more origin flavor. Dark roasts have more body and more bitterness.

buildup.text: Light roasts preserve the bean's acids—citric, malic, phosphoric—giving brightness and fruitiness.

discovery.text: Dark roasting breaks down those acids and develops smoky, chocolatey, carbony flavors from caramelization.

twist.text: Caffeine barely changes during roasting. Dark roasts seem stronger but have roughly the same caffeine.

climax.text: Neither is objectively better. Light highlights terroir; dark highlights technique. Both have devoted fans.

punchline.text: Light for origin, dark for body. Pick your priority.

quiz.question: Do dark roasts have more caffeine than light roasts?
options: No, caffeine levels are roughly the same

details.summary: Light roasts preserve origin character with bright acidity and complex fruity or floral notes. Dark roasts emphasize body, bitterness, and smoky caramel flavors while obscuring origin character. Contrary to myth, light roasts contain slightly more caffeine by weight than dark roasts.
details.whyItMatters: Roast level is the most visible choice in coffee. Understanding it helps consumers choose beans that match their taste preferences instead of guessing.
takeaways: Light roasts highlight origin flavors and acidity
Dark roasts emphasize body, bitterness, and caramel notes
Light roasts have slightly more caffeine by weight

faq.question: Which roast level has more caffeine?
faq.answer: Light roasts have slightly more caffeine per gram because roasting breaks down a small amount of caffeine. However, the difference is minimal. Brewing method and dose have far more impact on caffeine content than roast level.

faq.question: Why does specialty coffee favor lighter roasts?
faq.answer: Lighter roasts let unique origin characteristics and processing flavors shine through. Dark roasting homogenizes flavor, making different origins taste similar. Specialty roasters invest in high-quality beans and want their distinct qualities to be tasted.
